An elegant ivory-colored porcelain flower-arrangement vase designed by German sculptor and artist Karl Tutter (1883–1969) for Hutschenreuther, Germany, in 1965–1967. The piece features a refined, minimalist form with a smooth glossy surface, accented by a delicate gilded line along the rim.
Its central insert is crafted with neatly arranged openings, allowing for graceful floral displays. The design consists of two parts: a large bowl with holes around the edge for positioning cut flowers, and a central stand. The openings along the rim serve to secure stems in water, creating balanced and harmonious arrangements.
In very good condition, with no chips or cracks.
Diameter: 23 cm

Height: 5.5 cm

An antique tray produced by the renowned Swedish manufactory Gustavsberg at the turn of the 20th century (circa 1890–1910), during the Art Nouveau period. It is crafted from high-quality glazed faience, a material for which the factory was especially celebrated.
The tray is fitted with an elegant pierced metal gallery featuring a geometric design and graceful cast handles in the Art Nouveau style. Traditionally, it was used for serving desserts and sandwiches with tea or as a decorative vanity tray for perfume bottles.
Today, it is a highly collectible piece and an excellent example of early Scandinavian design.

Tray surface: 20 × 7.5 cm

Поднос оснащён изящной ажурной металлической галереей с геометрическим узором и литыми ручками в стиле модерн. Его использовали для десертов и сэндвичей к чаю или как туалетный поднос для флаконов духов.
Сегодня это востребованная коллекционная вещь и прекрасный образец раннего скандинавского дизайна.
Общие размеры: 23,5 × 8,5 × 3,5 см
Поверхность подноса: 20 × 7,5 см

Das Tablett hat eine elegante durchbrochene Metallgalerie mit geometrischem Muster und gegossene Jugendstilgriffe. Es diente zum Servieren von Gebäck und Sandwiches zum Tee oder als Frisiertablett für Parfümflakons.
